consensus_summary: Consensus treats 'seed' as multivalent with two leading, non-exclusive primaries: (1) the Word of God/gospel sown into human hearts (Jesus' own interpretation of the sower parable) and (2) offspring/descendants culminating in Christ (seed of the woman/Abraham). Secondary strands include mustard-seed faith, death-resurrection, sowing-reaping, and sons of the kingdom. Which strand is called primary depends on parabolic vs. redemptive-historical focus; both are universally recognized.
book_summary: The word of God, sown in the hearts of men.
consensus_core_identification: Word of God/gospel (parable of the sower) or messianic offspring (Christ as seed of woman/Abraham), both dominant and context-dependent.
book_core_identification: The word of God sown in the hearts of men.
boundary_disagreement: None material. Book simply presents one of the two leading consensus strands without redefining its cases or denying the other.
rationale: Book's wording is essentially identical to the primary meaning given in consensus responses A and C and listed as dominant alternative in B and D. The identification rests on the same explicit dominical definition (Luke 8:11) that consensus treats as authoritative for the parabolic sense. Variation among the blind responses over ranking (Word vs. messianic seed) is internal to consensus and does not create divergence; both strands coexist without contradiction. Book's omission of alternatives is immaterial detail, not a changed core or boundary.
strongest_objection: Book presents only the parabolic Word-of-God sense and therefore under-emphasizes the messianic seed-of-the-woman/Abraham strand that several consensus responses rank as equally or more theologically central across the canon.
